newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU's Spring heads for Israel, Gaza for peace talks.
newsitem.headline: EU's Spring heads for Israel, Gaza for peace talks.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring heads for Israel and Gaza on Sunday on a peace mission ordered by European Union leaders frustrated and angry at being cut out of U.S.-brokered peace efforts.
Irish officials said Spring would convey the EU's desire to see the Israelis and Palestinians to make further efforts to patch up a peace process damaged by renewed violence.
Ireland currently holds the rotating EU presidency and European leaders were meeting in Dublin for a special summit.

But it was not clear whether Spring's message would be the same as a tough EU statement issued on Tuesday, which called on Israel to match its stated desire for peace with actions to fulfil its obligations.
Officials said they did not yet know whether Spring would pay a potentially controversial visit to the Palestinian Authority's Orient House offices in disputed East Jerusalem.
"We are still making logistical arrangements and it is not yet decided where he will go and who he will see," one said.

It is EU policy for foreign ministers to hold meetings with the Palestinian Authority in Orient House when visiting the Middle East. But Israel has signalled it would strongly disapprove of any EU visit to the offices, which it would see as backing for Palestinian claims to East Jerusalem.

Israel has raised the possibility that it would refuse to meet EU representatives if they visited Orient House. Spring paid a visit to Orient House in 1995 and was promptly snubbed by the Israeli president, who cancelled planned talks.
Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said Israel was already unhappy with the EU over Tuesday's strongly-worded statement.
"That put us in a very difficult and uncomfortable situation," he added.
Officials said there were indications that the U.S. was also unenthusiastic about EU efforts to secure a more significant role in the peace process.
Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat appealed this week for more EU involvement in the peace effort.

But some EU diplomats said in Dublin they had been told that U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher had sent a letter to the EU which appeared to suggest it should not become too involved in the current peace drive.
Spring said the EU had made it clear it wanted to play a part. "We have had a dialogue with the U.S. this week. They know we want to be involved," he told Irish RTE television.

Announcing Spring's peace mission, Irish Prime Minster John Bruton told a news conference on Saturday it was appropriate for the EU to play a significant role, particularly since it was by far the largest donor of humanitarian and development aid in support of the peace process.

Bruton said they had also discussed the appointment of a special envoy to the region, who would ensure a longer-term EU involvement in Middle East affairs. He said the envoy would probably concentrate on economic issues.

Israel and the Palestinian Authority hold talks at the Israeli border on Sunday. They are expected to discuss the closure of an archeological tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem whose opening sparked violence which killed 73 people.
Asked whether Spring would press for the closure of the tunnel, Bruton said the full details of the EU's message had not yet been decided.
